chapter_title: Day 11: Athens, the Agora, Democracy, and Paul on the Areopagus
learning_objective: The learner will classify nine jobs of Athenian public life by the Agora building or monument where each was done, choosing correctly for at least 7 of 9 on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** agora-democracy-workplaces
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify nine jobs of Athenian public life by the Agora building or monument where each was done, choosing correctly for at least 7 of 9 on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Ancient Agora of Athens, stoa, Royal Stoa, Metroon, Bouleuterion, Tholos, Monument of the Eponymous Heroes, Stoa Poikile, Stoa of Attalos, Temple of Hephaestus, Council of 500, trial of Socrates (all defined in Parts One and Two above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each job card the learner selects one place on the plan before feedback. A choice is correct when it matches the Correct place column in Content. Mastery is 7 of 9 correct on the first attempt, including card 5 (the impiety charge), where the likely wrong answer is a law court. Clicking a place to read its description is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The Agora was only a market (cards 1, 2, 3, 4). (2) Trials started in a courtroom, when charges of impiety were filed with the King Archon at the Royal Stoa (card 5). (3) Philosophy was taught in schools with buildings, when the Stoics met in a public stoa (card 7). (4) The Stoa of Attalos dates from Socrates' time, when it was built about 250 years later (card 8). **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying jobs by building makes the learner reconstruct the Agora as a working system of government rather than a field of foundations. Showing the places on a schematic plan, by side of the square, ties each job to where it stands on our walk. **Content:** A schematic plan of the Agora, not to scale, showing the open square with the Panathenaic Way crossing it diagonally from the northwest corner to the southeast, and ten places, each with a short description revealed on click: | Place | Position on the plan | Description revealed on click | |---|---|---| | Royal Stoa | West side, north end, beside the metro tracks | Office of the King Archon, who handled religious law. | | Stoa of Zeus Eleutherios | West side, south of the Royal Stoa | A stoa to Zeus the Freedom-Giver; ancient writers name it as a favorite spot for Socrates' conversations. | | Metroon | West side, middle | The city archive, where laws and decrees were stored. | | Bouleuterion | Behind the Metroon, on the west side | The meeting hall of the Council of 500. | | Monument of the Eponymous Heroes | On the open square, in front of the Metroon | Bronze statues of the ten tribal heroes; public notices were posted on its base. | | Tholos | West side, south end | Round building where the 50 councillors on duty dined at public expense. | | Boundary stone | Southwest corner | Marble stone of about 500 BCE: "I am the boundary of the Agora." | | Stoa Poikile | North side, beyond the metro tracks | The Painted Stoa of the 460s BCE, with paintings of Marathon; Zeno taught here. | | Stoa of Attalos | East side | Two-story stoa of 42 shops, a gift of Attalos II about 150 BCE; rebuilt 1953–1956 as the museum. | | Temple of Hephaestus | On the low hill above the west side | Doric temple of Hephaestus and Athena, patrons of crafts, begun about 449 BCE. | Job cards, in this order: | # | Job card | Correct place | Reason shown after answering | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Read a proposed new law, or check whether you have been called up for the army. | Monument of the Eponymous Heroes | Notices were posted on its base, where every citizen passed. | | 2 | Prepare the agenda for the next Assembly. | Bouleuterion | The Council of 500 met here to prepare the Assembly's business. | | 3 | Eat dinner at public expense as one of the 50 councillors on duty. | Tholos | The councillors on duty dined here, and some stayed overnight so the city always had a government awake. | | 4 | Look up the exact wording of a decree passed years ago. | Metroon | It was the city's archive of laws and decrees. | | 5 | File a charge of impiety, as Meletus did against Socrates. | Royal Stoa | Impiety was religious law, so the charge went to the King Archon's office before any trial. | | 6 | Sit in the shade and talk with Socrates, as ancient writers describe. | Stoa of Zeus Eleutherios | Ancient writers name this stoa as a favorite spot for Socrates' conversations. | | 7 | Hear Zeno teach beside the painting of Marathon. | Stoa Poikile | Zeno taught in the Painted Stoa, and his followers were named Stoics after it. | | 8 | Buy goods in a shop given by a king of Pergamon who had studied in Athens. | Stoa of Attalos | Attalos II paid for its 42 shops about 150 BCE, two and a half centuries after Socrates. | | 9 | Pray to the god of the forge above the bronze workshops. | Temple of Hephaestus | Hephaestus, with Athena, was the patron of the craftsmen around the Agora. | The boundary stone has no job card; it is a place the learner can click but is never the answer. **Provenance:** Places, positions, dates, and descriptions from Part One ("The Ancient Agora of Athens," "The Stoa," "The Temple of Hephaestus") and Part Two ("Athenian Democracy," "The Trial of Socrates") of this chapter. Positions are schematic (side of the square), not measured; the plan is labeled "Schematic plan, not to scale." **Rules:** Each card is answered once for scoring. A first-attempt answer is correct if and only if it equals the Correct place. Score is 0 to 9. Mastery is score >= 7 with card 5 correct. Every place, including the boundary stone, can be selected for every card. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the plan with all ten places labeled and may click any place to read its description. 2. Card 1 appears. The learner selects the place where that job was done. 3. Feedback appears, and the card is pinned beside its correct place on the plan. 4. The learner continues through card 9. 5. At the end, the plan shows all nine jobs pinned. The learner should notice that six of the nine jobs cluster along the west side, the democracy's "street of offices." **Feedback:** After each first attempt: correct shows "Correct" and the reason; incorrect shows "This job belonged to the [correct place]: [reason]." After card 9: if mastery is met, "You can read the Agora as a working government."; otherwise, "Walk the west side again: archive, council, dining hall, notice board, and the King Archon's office." A Try Again option repeats all nine cards. **Starting State:** The labeled plan, no cards pinned, and card 1 with the question "Where in the Agora would you go to do this?" **Chapter Anchors:** Ten places; nine job cards; Council of 500; 50 councillors on duty; boundary stone of about 500 BCE; Stoa Poikile of the 460s BCE; Stoa of Attalos about 150 BCE with 42 shops, rebuilt 1953–1956; Temple of Hephaestus begun about 449 BCE; mastery 7 of 9.
